claim: Minting a page's id belongs to one change act rather than to the landing. `add-file` reaches `add-file-of-any-kind`, which puts a fresh uuid version 7 into any body that names a page and states no id. `add-page-property` composes the add of its property page itself and reaches that act nowhere, so the body lands exactly as the agent handed it in. A property page made that way states no id, and the check that a page matches its type refuses the fold, naming the page rather than the change that dropped the id. The agent then mints a uuid by hand, against the decision on `page/properties/id.text-property.ts` that a page being created states no id of its own.

evidence:
Run on the akasha checkout. `akasha change apply --draft add-page-property` at `domain/finding/properties/throwaway-probe.boolean-property.ts`, `part-of` and `on` both `domain/finding/finding.page-type.ts`, `required: false`, `many: false`, with a body stating no `id`. The draft was kept. `akasha change apply` with a message answered `the fold is undone` and, first among its lines, `domain/finding/properties/throwaway-probe.boolean-property.ts — does not state ``id``, which ``page-type/boolean-property`` requires`, then `domain/finding/finding.page-type.ts — states ``parts``, and no ``boolean-property`` carries the slug ``throwaway-probe```, the same for `properties page-property`, and a TS1360 saying the object does not satisfy `BooleanProperty`. Nothing was written.

The same body handed to `akasha change apply --draft add-file` at the same path drew none of those lines. `akasha change show` on the kept draft answered the body with `id: "01a0c4ec-f34b-7316-8bca-e525e9c91e99"` already in it, so the id goes in as the change act runs, before any landing. `akasha change show` on the `add-page-property` draft of the same path answered the body with no `id` line at all.

The act that mints is `addFileOfAnyKind`. Its `runChange` calls `idFilled` where `pagedAt(world, given.at)` holds, and `idFilled` mints with `uuidVersion7()` and writes it with `insertedInto`. Handing `add-file` an `id` of one space drew `an ``id`` stating nothing is no id, so ``id`` is left out or said as ``auto```, which is `idFilled`'s own refusal, so that function is on `add-file`'s road. `addPageProperty` ends `return stating([{ kind: "add", path: given.at, content: given.body }, ...edits])`, which is a raw add reaching `addFileOfAnyKind` nowhere. That is the whole condition: minting hangs off one act, not off the landing every act shares.

`mintingOnto` in `command/modules/value-minting/value-minting.module.code.ts` also fills a new page's generated properties, and it is not what mints here. Its only caller outside its own test is `tidiedIn` in `page/service/modules/page-writing/page-writing.module.code.ts`, the page service writer, which the `akasha change apply` road does not travel. Neither its `if ("refused" in cast) return NOTHING_MINTED` line nor `couldTurn` has any part in this refusal.

What makes it easy to miss: `page/properties/id.text-property.ts` states `generator: "generator-kind/uuid-v7"` and the decision `A page being created states no id of its own.`, which reads as a rule the whole system keeps, and `add-file` keeps it, so an agent who has ever made a page that way has evidence it is kept everywhere. The refusal names the page and its page type, not the change, so it reads as a body the agent wrote wrong. Re-running the same `add-page-property` call with a hand-minted `01a0c4ec-f34b-7316-8bca-e525e9c91e99` cleared that line and the two `parts` and `properties` lines with it, leaving only a TS2724 for the property's missing `.types.ts` export, which reads as confirmation that stating the id by hand was right.

The condition a mend would meet: every change act that adds a page reaches the one act that mints a page's id, so an agent composing a property page states no id and is refused for no id in the same repository.
